newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST-Japan Nov money growth seen flat to lower.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Japan Nov money growth seen flat to lower.

text.p: Growth of Japan's broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (M2+CDs), the key gauge of money supply, is expected to be steady to slightly lower in November compared with October, economists said on Monday.
Economists polled by Reuters in Tokyo gave predictions ranging from 3.4 percent to 3.7 percent in November from a year earlier.
In October, money supply grew a preliminary 3.7 percent from a year earlier. The data will be released by the Bank of Japan at 8.50 a.m. on Wednesday (2350 GMT on Tuesday).
Economists said corporations have been shying away from bank loans in favour of the capital markets where they can raise funds cheaply and flexibly, which could keep money supply growth in check.
But higher than usual deposit withdrawals from postal savings in November and a shift of funds to time deposits at commercial banks could contribute to a money supply increase, they said.
Mamoru Yamaguchi, an economist at Nikko Research Center, said money growth is likely to slow down slightly in November due to a reaction to its sharp rise a year ago.
Money supply grew sharply in November 1995 because investors had shifted a portion of their maturing funds to commercial bank deposits.
"Since we did not have such a money-boosting factor this year, there would be a reaction (to the sharp increase a year earlier)," he added.
